[p. 540]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Hadid.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

We have mentioned many times that tasbih (glorifying, declaring Allah free of imperfection) is to declare Allah transcendent above everything that does not befit His perfection and majesty. Its root in the language is distancing from evil, from the saying of the Arabs, "sabaha" when he became far away. From this comes the name for a horse, sabih, because when it runs it moves away swiftly. From this is the saying of 'Antarah in his mu'allaqa (one of the celebrated pre-Islamic odes):

"While I still remain upon a deep-chested, swift saddled horse, which the warriors strike repeatedly, wounded."

And the saying of 'Abbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami:

"They do not plant palm shoots around them, nor do the cows low in their winter pens,
Except swift ones like eagles, brought near, in an enclosure around which are dangers and cares."

This verb, "sabbaha", may take its object directly without the lam, as in His saying: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾ [al-Ahzab: 42], and His saying: ﴿And during the night prostrate to Him and glorify Him through a long night﴾ [al-Insan: 26]. It may also take the lam, as in His saying here: "sabbaha li-Allah." Accordingly, "sabbahahu" and "sabbaha lahu" are two forms, like "nasahahu" and "nasaha lahu," and "shakarahu" and "shakara lahu." Some scholars have mentioned another meaning for the verse: that the sense is ﴿whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah﴾, i.e., it brings about tasbih for the sake of Allah, seeking His countenance, the exalted. This was mentioned by al-Zamakhshari and Abu Hayyan. It has also been said that "sabbaha li-Allah" means "prayed to Him."

We have mentioned that tasbih is applied to prayer. What this noble verse contains, that the people of the heavens and the earth glorify Allah, meaning they declare Him free of what does not befit Him, has been clarified by Allah, majestic and exalted, in other verses of His Book, such as:

• His saying in Surat al-Hashr: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [al-Hashr: 1] and so on.

• His saying in al-Saff: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [al-Saff: 1] and so on.

• His saying in al-Jumu'ah: ﴿Glorifying Allah is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, the King, the Holy, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 1] and so on.

• His saying in al-Taghabun: ﴿Glorifying Allah is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth; to Him belongs dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Taghabun: 1] and so on.

In Surat Bani Isra'il, He added that the seven heavens and the earth glorify Allah, along with whatever is in them, [p. 541] of creation, and that the glorification of the heavens and the like among inanimate things is known to Allah, while we do not comprehend it, i.e., we do not understand it. This is in His saying: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra': 44]. This noble verse clearly shows that the glorification of inanimate things mentioned in it, and in His saying: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with David﴾ [al-Anbiya': 79], and similar verses, is a real glorification, known to Allah, while we do not know it.

This noble verse contains a clear refutation of those among the people of knowledge who claim that the glorification of inanimate things is the indication that their existence points to the power of their Creator. The reason is that the indication of created beings to the greatness of their Creator is understood by all people of intellect, as Allah, exalted, has stated in His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, and the ships that sail through the sea with that which benefits people…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164]. Similar verses are numerous in the Qur'an.

We have already explained this in Surat al-Ra'd in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows [prostrate] in the mornings and evenings﴾ [al-Ra'd: 15] and so on; in Surat al-Kahf in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And they found within it a wall that wanted to collapse﴾ [al-Kahf: 77] and so on; and in Surat al-Ahzab in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72], and in other places.

Here at the beginning of al-Hadid, Allah has used the past form in His saying: ﴿sabbaha li-Allah﴾ [al-Hadid: 1], and likewise in al-Hashr and al-Saff. In al-Jumu'ah, al-Taghabun, and others, He used the present form, "yusabbihu."

Some scholars said: He used the past form in some places and the present form in others to show that this glorification of Allah is the custom and habit of the people of the heavens and the earth, in the past and the future. This meaning was mentioned by al-Zamakhshari and Abu Hayyan.

His saying: ﴿And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [al-Hadid: 1]. We have mentioned its meaning many times, and we mentioned that al-'Aziz is the Overpowering, whom nothing overpowers, and that 'izza (might) is domination. From this is His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs might, and to His Messenger﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8], and the saying: "wa-'azzani fi al-khitab," meaning, he overpowered me in the dispute. Among the proverbs of the Arabs: "Whoever is mighty plunders," meaning whoever overpowers, seizes. From this is the saying of al-Khansa':

"As if they had never been a protected sanctuary feared, when people then were: whoever was mighty plundered."

Al-Hakim is the one who places matters in their proper places and brings them into their proper positions.

His saying: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 1]: here the non-rational is given precedence. We have mentioned elsewhere that Allah sometimes gives precedence to the non-rational, as in "whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth," because of its abundance, and sometimes gives precedence to the rational because of its importance. An example combining both is His saying in al-Baqarah: ﴿Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 116] and so on. Here He gave precedence to the non-rational in His saying "whatever is in the heavens," and gave precedence to the rational in His saying "qanitun" (devoutly obedient).

**The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 57, verse 4:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne﴾.

As for His saying ﴿in six days﴾ [al-Hadid: 4], we have already explained it in Surah Fussilat, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days?﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾, and the verses that follow [al-Fussilat: 9–12]. We also explained it in Surah al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾, and the verse [al-A'raf: 54].

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿then established Himself upon the Throne﴾ [al-Hadid: 4], we have already presented the many verses that clarify it in Surah al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿then established Himself upon the Throne; He covers the night with the day﴾, and the verse [al-A'raf: 54]. We also mentioned a good portion of that in Surah al-Qital (Muhammad), in our lengthy discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it﴾. We have already explained it at the beginning of Surah Saba', in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving﴾, and the verse [Saba': 2].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾.

We have already explained it, and we clarified the Qur'anic verses that indicate the general companionship (al-ma'iyyah al-'ammah) and the special companionship (al-ma'iyyah al-khassah), together with an explanation of the meaning of companionship, at the end of Surah al-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: (p-543) ﴿Indeed Allah is with those who are mindful of Him and those who are doers of good﴾, and the verse [al-Nahl: 128].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab, "Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book"):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Hadid.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿then established Himself upon the Throne﴾.

It indicates that He, may He be exalted, is established upon His Throne, high above all His creation. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [57: 4], appears to indicate otherwise.

The answer is that He, may He be exalted, is established upon His Throne as He said, without how (bila kayf) and without likeness (bila tashbih), in a manner befitting His perfection and majesty. All creatures are in His hand smaller than a grain of mustard seed. He is with all of them by complete encompassing, perfect knowledge, and the penetrating power of His command, glorified and exalted be He far above that. There is therefore no contradiction between His being high upon His Throne and His companionship with all creatures.

Do you not see, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, that if one of us were to hold in his hand a grain of mustard seed, he would not be inside any part of that grain, although he encompasses all its parts and is with all its parts? The heavens and the earth and whoever is in them are in the hand of Allah, may He be exalted, smaller than a grain of mustard seed in the hand of one of us, and to Him belongs the highest likeness, glorified be He and exalted far above that. He is nearer to each one of us than the neck of his mount, indeed nearer than the jugular vein, and yet He is established upon His Throne, nothing of the deeds of His creatures is hidden from Him, Majestic and Exalted is He.

(p-544) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Maryam, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is on it.﴾ [Maryam: 40]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands, (it will be said to them): "Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. That is the great triumph."﴾

In this noble verse, exalted and majestic is He, He mentions that on the Day of Resurrection the believers' light will run before them and on their right hands (yamin is the plural of yamin, "right hand"), and that it will be said to them: ﴿Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. That is the great triumph﴾ [al-Hadid: 12].

What this noble verse contains of what we have mentioned has been clarified in other verses. As for the running of their light before them and on their right hands, Allah, exalted is He, has explained it in Surat al-Tahrim, and He added in it an explanation of the supplication they will make at that time, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light"﴾ — to the end of the verse [al-Tahrim: 8].

As for the glad tidings of the gardens given to them, it has come clarified in other places, and Allah has explained in them that the angels give them glad tidings and that their Lord also gives them glad tidings, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him and approval and gardens wherein they will have enduring pleasure﴾ ﴿abiding therein forever. Indeed, with Allah is a great reward﴾ [al-Tawbah: 21-22], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿as a hospitable gift from the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [Fussilat: 30-32], in addition to other verses.

The pronoun in "yunadunahum" (they call out to them) refers to the hypocrites, male and female, and the object pronoun refers to the believers, male and female. In this noble verse, Allah, Exalted is He, mentions that when the hypocrites, male and female, see the light of the believers on the Day of Resurrection going before them and on their right hands, they say to them: "Look at us, so that we may borrow from your light." It is said to them in reply: "Return behind you and seek light" (p-545). The Surah mentions that they call out to the believers: "Were we not with you?" That is, in the life of the world: we used to witness the prayers with you, march with you in the military expeditions (ghazawat), and follow your religion? They say: "Yes," meaning: you were with us in the life of the world, "but you tempted yourselves."

We have previously mentioned several times the meanings of fitnah (trial, temptation, discord) and its uses in the Qur'an, and we explained that among its meanings in the Qur'an is misguidance, such as disbelief and sins. This is what is intended here: "fattantum anfusakum" means you misguided yourselves, by means of hypocrisy, which is inner disbelief. From this meaning is Allah's saying: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ [al-Anfal: 39], meaning until no polytheism remains, as was previously clarified. As for His saying: ﴿And you waited﴾ [al-Hadid: 14], al-tarabbus means waiting. The more evident view is that what is meant here is the hypocrites' waiting for the believers to suffer misfortunes, that is, their awaiting the calamities of time to destroy them, as in Allah's saying about the hypocrites among the Bedouins mentioned in His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾ [al-Tawbah: 101], and ﴿And among the Bedouins is he who takes what he spends as a fine and awaits misfortunes for you. Upon them is the misfortune of evil﴾ [al-Tawbah: 98].

His saying: "And you doubted," meaning you were in doubt about the religion of Islam. Their doubt mentioned here, and their disbelief resulting from it, is explained by Allah's saying about them: ﴿Only those seek your permission who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt, so they are hesitating in their doubt﴾ [al-Tawbah: 45].

His saying: ﴿And false hopes deceived you until the command of Allah came﴾ [al-Hadid: 14]. Al-amani is the plural of umniyyah, which is what they wish for themselves of falsehood, such as their claim that they are reformers in their hypocrisy, and that the truly believing are fools in their sincerity, that is, in their faith. This is as Allah, Exalted, explained in His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers." Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters﴾ [al-Baqarah: 11–12], up to the end of the verse, and His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Should we believe as the fools have believed?" Unquestionably, it is they who are the fools﴾ [al-Baqarah: 13], up to the end of the verse.

That which this noble verse includes, namely that the aforementioned false hopes are among the delusions by which they were deceived, has been made clear in other places, such as Allah's saying: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and they will not be wronged the amount of a speck﴾ [al-Nisa': 123–124].

His saying: ﴿until the command of Allah came﴾ [al-Hadid: 14]. The more evident view is that this is death, because deeds end with it.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿And the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah﴾ [al-Hadid: 14]: the Deceiver is Satan (al-Shaytan), and he is described with the intensive form, which is al-ghurur (the one who deceives greatly), because of the abundance of his deception of the children of Adam, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾ [al-Isra': 64].

What He, Exalted is He, mentioned in this noble verse, that Satan, the great deceiver, deceived them concerning Allah, has been made clear in other verses, such as His saying at the end of Luqman: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life deceive you, and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ [Fatir: 5], and His saying at the beginning of Fatir: ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life deceive you, and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah. Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [Fatir: 5–6].

His saying in the two verses mentioned, of Luqman and Fatir, ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾ [Yunus: 55], and His placing the prohibition against being deceived concerning Allah by the Deceiver after it, is clear evidence that among what Satan deceives them with is the claim that Allah's promise of resurrection is not true, and that it will not happen. And al-ghurur, with a dammah, means deception.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So on that Day no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Ali 'Imran, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Never will be accepted from any of them an earth full of gold even if he ransomed himself with it﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 91], and in other places besides that.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 57, verse 16:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah and to what has descended of the truth, and that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term grew long for them so their hearts hardened? And many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾

We have mentioned several times that every present-tense verb (*mudari'*, the imperfect) in the Qur'an that is jussive (*majzum*) with *lam* (the negative particle "not"), when preceded by the interrogative hamza (*hamzat al-istifham*), as here, has two well-known interpretations.

The first of them: its present-tense form is turned into the past, and its negation into affirmation, so that it carries the meaning of the affirmed past. This is because *lam* is a particle that turns the present from the sense of the future to the sense of the past, and the interrogative hamza is a denial (*inkariyyah*), containing the sense of negation. Thus the implicit negation within it governs the explicit negation in *lam*, negating it, and the negation of a negation is an affirmation, so the meaning returns to the affirmed past. Accordingly, the meaning of "Has the time not come for those who..." is: the time has come for those who believe.

The second interpretation: the interrogation in all of this is for affirmation (*taqrir*), which means leading the addressee to acknowledge, so that he says: "Yes." The phrase "yet'in" (*ya'ni*) is the imperfect of *anā yaʾnī* (the verb meaning "to arrive"), when it comes with its *inā'* (its appointed time), meaning its time. From it is the saying of Ka'b ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him:

*"And indeed it has come to you (anā laka) that you should desist willingly, or repent when the guide forbids you."*

So his saying *"anā laka an tatanāhā ṭā'iʿan"* means: the appointed time (*al-inā'*), which is the time in which you desist willingly, has come; that is, the time of your desisting has arrived. In Arabic one says *ā'na yaʾīnu* (the verb in the form *fa'ala yaf'ilu*), like *bāʿa yabīʿu*, and *anā yaʾnī* like *ramā yarmī*. The statement of the poet combines both dialects:

*"Has it not yet come to me (ya'in li) that my blindness be cleared, and that I refrain from Layla? Yes indeed, it has come for me (qad anā lī)."*

The meaning according to both views is that it has become due for the believers, and that the time has come for their hearts to humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah; that is, the appointed time and the season for that have arrived, because of the abundance of the Qur'an's admonitions and exhortations that have repeatedly come to them.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿that their hearts should humble themselves﴾, the verbal noun formed from *an* (that) and its clause, is in the place of the subject (*fa'il*) of the verb *yaʾni*. *Khushū'* (humbling oneself) in the language originally means stillness, tranquility and lowering. From it is the saying of Nābigha Dhubyānī:

*"Ash like the kohl of the eye, a remnant I make out (la'yan), and a pit like the stump of a pool, worn and humbled (khāshi')."*

Thus his saying *"khāshi'"* means lowered, tranquil. In the Sharia, *khushū'* is a fear of Allah that penetrates the hearts, and its effects appear on the limbs through lowering and stillness, as is the condition of one who is afraid.

As for his saying: ﴿for the remembrance of Allah﴾, the more apparent meaning of it is that what is intended is the humbling of their hearts for the sake of the remembrance of Allah. This meaning is indicated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾ [al-Anfal: 2]; that is, they are frightened when Allah is mentioned. So the *wajal* (trembling) mentioned in this verse of al-Anfal and the *khashya* (fear) mentioned here have the same meaning.

Some scholars said: what is meant by the remembrance of Allah is the Qur'an. According to this view, His saying: ﴿and what has descended of the truth﴾ is an instance of conjoining a thing with itself while the two expressions differ, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who decreed and guided﴾ [al-A'la: 1–3], as we have explained several times.

On this view, the verse is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and repetitive, whereat shiver the skins of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Zumar: 23]. The shivering mentioned, and the softening of skins and hearts at the hearing of this great Qur'an, described as "the best statement," explains the meaning of humbling oneself to the remembrance of Allah, and "what has descended of the truth" here is as mentioned.

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term grew long for them so their hearts hardened﴾, we have already mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah, in discussing His saying: ﴿Then your hearts hardened﴾ [al-Baqarah: 74], some of the causes of the hardening of their hearts. We mentioned among them the lengthening of the term mentioned here in this verse of al-Hadid, and other causes in some other verses.

As for what this noble verse contains regarding the abundance of the defiantly disobedient among the People of the Book, it is clarified in other verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Had the People of the Book believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Had the People of the Book believed, it would have been better for them...﴾ [al-Hadid: 27] (as in the text given), and other verses besides these.

The Almighty's statement: ﴿Like the example of rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers, then it dries up and you see it turning yellow, then it becomes debris﴾.

We have already discussed this in Surat al-Zumar, in our discussion of His statement: ﴿Then it dries up, and you see it turning yellow; then He makes it debris﴾ [Az-Zumar: 21], and we explained there the verse that indicates the cause of its yellowing.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿No calamity befalls on earth or among yourselves except that it is in a Book before We bring it into being. Indeed that, for Allah, is easy.﴾

In this noble verse, He - majestic and exalted - mentions that every calamity that befalls on earth, such as drought, barrenness and blights affecting crops and fruits, and among the selves, such as sicknesses and death, is all written in a Book before the creation of people and before the existence of calamities. So His saying ﴿before We bring it into being﴾ [al-Hadid: 22], the pronoun in it refers either to the creation (al-khaliqah) implied within His saying ﴿nor among yourselves﴾ [al-Hadid: 22], or to the calamity, and some scholars chose that it refers to all of that.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed that, for Allah, is easy﴾ [al-Hadid: 22], meaning: easy and effortless, due to the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and the perfection of His power.

What this noble verse includes, that no calamity befalls people except that it is written with Allah before that - Allah, may He be exalted, clarified it in other than this place,

• like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Nothing will ever happen to us except what Allah has decreed for us. He is our Protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ [al-Tawbah: 51],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah﴾ [al-Taghabun: 11],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 155], because His saying: ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger﴾ [al-Baqarah: 155] before its occurrence is evidence that these calamities are known to Him - may He be exalted - before they occur. Therefore He informed them that they would occur, so that they would be prepared for them at the time they descend upon them, because that helps them to be patient with them.

The loss of wealth and fruits is among what befalls as calamity, and the loss of lives in His saying "and lives" is among what befalls as a calamity to the selves. His saying in this verse of al-Hadid: ﴿So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult over what He has given you﴾ [al-Hadid: 23], meaning: We have made clear to you that things are predestined and written before the existence of creation, and that what has been written certainly comes to pass, so that you do not grieve over something that has escaped you, because its escaping you is predestined, and one who has no hope in something has less sorrow over it; and do not exult over what He has given you, because when you know that what has been written for you of provision and good must reach you, your joy in it diminishes. His saying "ta'saw" is the imperfect of asiya (أسِيَ), with kasra in the sin, yaʾsa (يَأْسى) with fatha, asan (أسًى) with two fathas by analogy, meaning "grieved" (ḥazina). From it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 68]. His saying "min musibah" (مِن مُصِيبَةٍ) is in the genitive case in a position of nominative, because it is the subject of "asāba" (أصابَ), placed in the genitive by the extra "min" (مِنَ) for emphasizing the negation, and "ma" (ما) is a negation particle.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance, that people may maintain justice﴾.

We have already discussed this in surah al-Shura, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Allah is He who sent down the Scripture with truth and the balance﴾ [al-Shura: 17], and we have there presented the statements of the people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) concerning its meaning.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾.

In this noble verse and the one before it, Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, has made clear that the establishment of the religion of Islam rests upon two matters. The first is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We sent down with them the Scripture and the balance﴾ [al-Hadid: 25], because in that is the establishment of proofs for the truth, the clarification of the argument, and the explanation of the command, the prohibition, the reward and the punishment. If the disbelievers persist in unbelief and in denying the messengers despite that clarification and explanation, then Allah, blessed and exalted, sent down iron, that is, He created it for the sons of Adam, so that the believers might deter the stubborn disbelievers with it, namely by killing them with swords, spears and arrows. Accordingly, His saying here: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾ [al-Hadid: 25] is clarified by many verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So strike [them] upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip﴾ [al-Anfal: 12]. Verses of this kind are numerous and well known.

As for His saying: ﴿and benefits for mankind﴾ [al-Hadid: 25], the benefits of iron for people are not hidden. Allah has pointed to this in His saying: ﴿And of that which they heat in the fire seeking an ornament or a commodity﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17], because what is heated in the fire seeking a commodity is iron.

The Qur'anic phrase: ﴿So among them is one who is guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾

The author says: We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat az-Zukhruf, in the discussion of His words, ﴿And He made it a word remaining among his descendants that they might return.﴾ ﴿Rather, I gave enjoyment to these [people and their fathers] until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 28-29].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 28:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and will forgive you. And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾

We have already explained that the verified position is that this noble verse of Surat al-Hadid concerns the believers of this Ummah, that its context is clear on this, and that whoever among the people of knowledge claims that it refers to the People of the Book has erred. Moreover, what Allah has promised the believers of this Ummah is greater than what He promised the believers among the People of the Book, who were given their reward twice, as He said concerning them: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believe in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it." Those will be given their reward twice﴾ [al-Qasas: 52–54], and the rest of the verse.

The fact that what He promised the believers of this Ummah is greater is that giving the People of the Book their reward twice gave the believers of this Ummah the like of it, as He explained by His saying: ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾ [al-Hadid: 28]. And He added to them by His saying: ﴿and will appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and will forgive you﴾ [al-Hadid: 28].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 57, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that grace is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great grace.﴾

What this noble verse contains, that grace is in the hand of Allah alone and that He gives it to whom He wills, has come clarified (p-551) in many verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if He touches you with good, then there is no repeller of His grace.﴾ [Yunus: 107].

We have already presented the verses that clarify it at the beginning of Surah Fatir, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever Allah grants to the people of mercy, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him.﴾ [Fatir: 2].
